beats.html:
The first Labor Day parade
was September 5, 1882.

10,000 workers marched
through New York.

They were not given
the day off.
They took it.

Every one of them
lost a day's pay
to be there.

Somebody you know thinks
the weekend was a gift.
It was an invoice.

beats.html:
Halloween was never
about fear.

It grew out of Samhain,
the Gaelic festival marking
the end of harvest.

The night the year turned
and the boundary
went thin.

People needed a ritual
for the part of the year
that gets dark.

Somebody you know is
dreading the dark months.
This one is for them.

beats.html:
Labor Day is in September
on purpose.

The rest of the world
marks workers on May 1.

May 1 is tied to Chicago's
Haymarket affair of 1886,
and the men hanged after it.

A September date
let the country celebrate
without remembering.

Somebody you know says
it's just a long weekend.
Now you know what it cost.

beats.html:
Are You Afraid of the Dark
started in 1992.

The whole format was
children telling each other
stories in the woods.

No adult ever explained it.
No adult ever arrived
to make it safe.

The scary part was never
the monster. It was being
trusted with the story.

Somebody you know watched
this at a sleepover.
They still remember which one.

beats.html:
Goosebumps started
in 1992.

R.L. Stine was writing them
at roughly one a month.

Fast, cheap, for children,
and dismissed by
every serious critic.

It taught a generation
that a short chapter ending
on a hook is worth finishing.

Somebody you know learned
to read from these.
Not from the good books.

beats.html:
Disney would not put
its name on
The Nightmare Before Christmas.

It came out in 1993
under Touchstone.

They thought it was
too dark and too strange
for the Disney label.

It is now the thing
they sell you
every single October.

Somebody you know is
hiding the strange one.
That is usually the good one.

beats.html:
Nightmare named
a specific thing.

A mare was a spirit
believed to sit
on a sleeper's chest.

The weight. The paralysis.
The certainty something
is in the room.

People had a word for it
centuries before
they had an explanation.

Somebody you know has
woken up unable to move.
It has always had a name.
